findings.title: Deposit is within the amount cap
findings.detail: This amount check does not verify deposit protection or authenticity. Annual rent GBP 15600; cap = 15600 / 52 * 5 (GBP 1500.00 rounded down to pennies); requested GBP 1500. Importance: 85/100. Conditional: Confirm that the rented property is in England. Confirm this is an ordinary private tenancy, not an excluded arrangement. Confirm that rent and deposit cover the same whole tenancy. This is a limited amount-cap pass, not a finding of breach. On the supplied figures, rent of GBP 1300 per calendar month gives annual rent of GBP 15,600. Five weeks of that is GBP 1,500.00, which equals the stated deposit of GBP 1,500, so the amount is not above the cap. Nothing in the contract contradicts the figures or shows that the deposit covers a different tenancy or share. The cap applies only to covered tenancies, and the jurisdiction and tenancy type are unknown. The property is in London W12, but the context does not confirm England or an ordinary private tenancy. Those scope facts stay open, so the result remains conditional. Passing the cap says nothing about deposit protection or authenticity. Sources: https://www.gov.uk/guidance/tenant-fees-act-2019-guidance-for-tenants

findings.title: Managing agent appointment attachment not supplied
findings.detail: The contract refers to a separate attachment about the owner's appointment of the managing agent, which is not in the supplied evidence bundle. This means it was not found in the supplied material; it does not show that it does not exist or that anything is unlawful. The document should be requested. Importance: 45/100. Conditional: Content and materiality of the attachment are unknown. It is unknown whether another supplied document contains this material. The referenced material was not found in the supplied contract. Paragraph 11 refers to a separate attachment about the owner's appointment of the managing agent, and the bundle says it is not included. No other segment supplies that material. The contract has no appendix under a different heading that could stand in for it. Its contents and materiality are unknown, so the absence neither proves a breach nor shows the document does not exist. The issue stays conditional until the attachment is supplied and the affected clauses can be rechecked.
